- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction, especially after sharp spikes.
- After a price spike (e.g., >73), model often overshoots downward in next 5–10 days; reduce forecast slope slightly to allow for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price drops sharply, model underestimates further declines; add 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast tail.
- Model frequently underestimates true price drops after a 30-day forecast horizon; apply 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment to forecast if recent sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model lags in adjusting downward; apply early correction (e.g., 1–2 days ahead) to avoid prolonged overestimation.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to align with 30-day moving average of recent 10–15 days.
